standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the equality and the quasi-coherence in the scheme case, which is then pulled back to algebraic spaces.

core_obligations: Use the general discussion of representable higher direct images to reduce the statement for an affine morphism of algebraic spaces to the case of an affine morphism of schemes (proof lines 1914-1916).
Apply the scheme case to obtain both the identification $f_*\mathcal{F} \cong Rf_*\mathcal{F}$ as a quasi-coherent sheaf and the base change equality (proof lines 1916-1918).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the representable (scheme) case (proof lines 1914-1916).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that for an affine morphism the pushforward of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent and agrees with the derived pushforward, and that it commutes with base change (statement lines 1901-1911). The proof invokes the reduction to representable morphisms of algebraic spaces, which puts the question in the scheme case covered by the corresponding statement in Cohomology of Schemes. The reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
